title: ECC Enabled Reliable and Performant Processing-in-Memory
evidence_span: The institutional publication record describes a reliable bank-PIM architecture with tailored ECC for variable-retention-time scaling errors and multi-bit errors. It detects multi-bit errors and corrects at rank level while avoiding repetitive correction cost, uses a Codeword Flip method to mask VRT weak-cell errors, and applies odd-even bank pipelining. The abstract reports 90% PIM-unit utilization, up to 400x lower silent-data-corruption likelihood than traditional bank-PIM over five years, and potential 4x performance enhancement over rankPIM in selected microbenchmarks, with end-to-end LLM improvements.
problem: Processing-in-memory improves data locality but introduces reliability risks from variable-retention-time scaling errors, physical faults, and multi-bit errors that can cause silent data corruption or repeated rank-level correction overhead.
method_or_artifact: A reliable bank-PIM architecture with tailored rank-level ECC, Codeword Flip masking for VRT weak cells, and odd-even bank pipelining to preserve utilization while limiting correction interference.
workload_or_benchmark: PIM microbenchmarks and end-to-end LLM application evaluation; the institutional abstract reports comparisons with rankPIM and traditional bank-PIM.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Bank-level PIM integrated with modern DRAM, variable-retention-time weak cells, rank-level correction, and an odd-even bank pipeline; exact DRAM generation, fault distributions, and implementation cost require full-paper verification.
metrics: up to 400x lower five-year silent-data-corruption likelihood
potential 4x performance enhancement over rankPIM in selected microbenchmarks
limits: The evidence is an institutional publication record containing the abstract and DOI metadata, not a captured full paper. Exact ECC layouts, fault probabilities, correction latency, area/energy overhead, LLM configurations, and the meaning of the reported likelihood horizon require full-paper verification.
